frac.denominator>power.base.description: The base of a power in the denominator. If it is a variable, larger values push the whole function down.

frac.denominator>power.exponent.description: The degree of the power in the denominator. The larger the exponent, the faster the denominator grows and the more it suppresses the whole value.

sum.body>frac.denominator.description: The denominator of each term of the series. If it grows quickly, the series is likely to converge.

sum.body>frac.denominator>power.exponent.description: The exponent on the denominator of the series. If it is greater than 1, the series converges (p-series test).

sum.body>frac.numerator.description: The numerator of each term of the series.

integral.lower.description: An improper integral starting at negative infinity. It converges only if the integrand decays fast enough.

power.exponent>frac.numerator.description: The exponent is the numerator of a fraction. A fractional exponent as a whole denotes a root.

power.exponent>frac.denominator.description: The denominator of the exponent. A denominator of n is the same as an nth root.

frac.numerator>frac.numerator.description: A fraction is nested inside another fraction. It expresses a compound ratio.

frac.denominator>frac.denominator.description: There is another fraction inside the denominator. Simplifying it turns the division into a multiplication.

integral.integrand>frac.numerator.description: The numerator of the fraction being integrated.

integral.integrand>frac.denominator.description: The denominator of the fraction being integrated. Partial fraction decomposition may help here.

limit.body>frac.numerator.description: The numerator of the fraction inside the limit. If it and the denominator both go to 0 or infinity, l'Hôpital's rule applies.

limit.body>frac.denominator.description: The denominator of the fraction inside the limit. If it and the numerator both go to 0 or infinity, l'Hôpital's rule applies.
